result.summary: This PR replaces mtime-based cache invalidation for depends' local_dir source tarballs with content-addressed hashing. It generates a normalized, reproducible tarball via a new CMake script and names it by its SHA256 hash, so identical trees produce the same archive and different worktrees sharing SOURCES_PATH no longer collide or reuse stale archives. The recipe hash propagation for package/dependent build IDs is kept unchanged.
result.problem: Depends currently uses `find -newer` mtime comparisons to decide whether to rebuild a local_dir source tarball, which the linked issue #35764 documents as unreliable: deletions, permission changes, symlink retargeting, clock skew, and shared SOURCES_PATH across worktrees can all cause a stale or wrong tarball to be reused, silently building the wrong sources.

open_concerns: Author raised an open design question about whether to fix the tarball mtime to 2000-01-01 (matching default_build_TOUCH) instead of the current 1970-01-01, unresolved
Cross-user archive reproducibility is explicitly called out as a separate, unaddressed consideration by the author

result.card: This PR replaces bitcoin-core depends' mtime-based cache invalidation for local_dir source tarballs with content-addressed hashing, fixing a documented bug (#35764) where shared SOURCES_PATH across worktrees can cause stale or wrong source tarballs to be silently reused. It generates deterministic, normalized tarballs via a new CMake script and keys them by SHA256 so identical trees hash identically and distinct trees coexist safely. Only one current package (native_libmultiprocess) uses local_dir, but the fix addresses a real correctness gap in depends' caching logic that the author documented with detailed failure scenarios and self-verified with a full guix build. The PR is a draft, needs rebase, and conflicts with two other open depends-related PRs (#36006, #35618), and no reviewer has yet engaged with the design, including an open question the author raised about the fixed archive mtime value.
